piece_title: W1-30E — architecture, settlements and the model kit (round 1 critique)

bifurcation.note: Declared before any frame was opened. This piece has two genuinely separate questions and they are scored without crossing: the ART-DIRECTION question is whether eight settlements read as eight places with their own architectural language (RI-WLD03, RI-VIS05, RI-VIS07, and the board's ART-SET-* rows); the FIDELITY question is whether the surfaces are made rather than blockout (the chamfer, trim and esCurvature work). No Morrowind plate was averaged with a modern one at any point.

score.band_label: The kit is real, economical and derived from the world's own vocabulary, and the 37 named cultural features survived rather than being rebuilt — the two strongest attacks this child's own plan predicted did not land. But its primary gate never executed because the eight street shots put the camera inside geometry, its skyline is destroyed at the approach by fog it does not own, and its roof-variety row fails under both readings.

status_reasons: The eight mandatory settlement street shots — the plan's own deciding gate for this child — put the camera inside building geometry in all three cases examined on hardware (Lilmoth, Helstrom, Gideon). The gate did not execute, and a critic may not pass a piece on a gate that did not run.
Ruling E1's silhouette reading is upheld but does not rescue the roof-profile row: the honest number moves from 1 to 3 against a bar of 5, minimum over settlements per Ruling W1.

E1's falsifier fires in exactly three settlements — Gideon (max pair IoU 0.9995), Stormhold and Blackrose (1.000) — where two 'distinct' roof classes are literally the same silhouette. In those towns the variety is parameter jitter.

Lilmoth's approach frame shows the skyline has real relief and that the fog at the approach camera removes the contrast it needs to read; the plan's >= 45% skyline-attribution row cannot be passed from inside exterior.js.
Helstrom's approach frame shows one wide hipped roof repeated across the town — the uniformity failure this child's own falsification audit predicted a kit would produce.
3,284 building meshes carry no kitId against a bar of zero. The builder's refusal to tag them is upheld as correct; the row fails because the work is not done, which the builder said.
The edges-are-broken row has no isolating single-variable null control: null:no-chamfer moves it 0.971 -> 0.9637 and leaves it passing.

biggest_gap.what: The eight settlement street shots, which the plan names as this child's deciding gate, place the camera inside building geometry. Lilmoth is filled by the courses of a single reed wall with no street visible; Helstrom is jammed against a stone wall with the player half-clipped into it; Gideon is a timber post filling the frame with the player entirely inside the wall. The one measurement that could confirm or refute this child has never executed.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: The kit's entire justification is how it reads at 4-8 m — the plan says so in its first paragraph, and the builder correctly refused to claim it from offline geometry. The offline proxies deliberately cannot answer it, the naive attribution packs are built from these frames, and the board's settlement rows are defined on them. So the gate, the human read and the board row all depend on eight camera positions that nobody had looked at because nobody had rendered a frame. This is the same shape as the defect the owner complained about: a claim standing on an instrument that was never pointed at the thing.

remedy.action: Move the 8 street-* setups in tools/visual/deck.json off the raw gameplay camera at yaw 270 and onto the settlement's own street centreline with a collision push-out. settlementApproach() in game/src/render/exterior.js already carries the settlement's approach vector and the plan carries every building footprint, so the push-out has the data it needs. Then re-run the child-scoped profile and score the row. This is a W1-30V edit, not a W1-30E one, and it should be dispatched there.
remedy.acceptance: All 8 street frames show at least 2 buildings whose facades are visible and unoccluded, with the near facade between 4 and 8 m from the camera, and zero frames in which the player capsule intersects building geometry. Re-measured by re-running the 8 street setups and checking the depth buffer's nearest non-player surface is >= 1.5 m in every frame.

secondary_observations.what: RULING E1, ruled on. Part (a): E1's reading is UPHELD. Its falsifier's condition is that the variety is parameter jitter reading as noise, and it is not — five of eight settlements carry five or more roof silhouettes mutually distinct by a wide margin (median pair IoU 0.50-0.74 in helstrom, lilmoth and archon). The ruling's reasoning is also right on its own terms: three roof parts cannot yield five roof PARTS per settlement without breaking the 25-part cap in the same plan, and a row no build can satisfy is a defect in the row. Part (b): the row STILL FAILS under E1's own reading. Aggregating minimum-over-settlements per Ruling W1 (a player walks into one town), the worst is 3 against a bar of 5. E1 changes what the number means; it does not change the verdict. Part (c): the falsifier DOES fire, precisely, in Gideon, Stormhold and Blackrose — the three grammars with roofMix [1] — where two 'distinct' classes overlap at 0.9995, 1.000 and 1.000. The builder's own proposed rescue is worse than E1's: it offers 32 distinct silhouettes in Lilmoth, but those are whole-BUILDING silhouettes including storey count and footprint, which would pass the row while the roofs stayed identical. Remedy: give roof.hip a discrete gable/monopitch flag — the same part, one boolean in the spec, two genuinely different silhouettes — and put it in the three failing grammars' mixes. That is a variant, not a part, so the 25-part economy is untouched. Re-run the falsifier; the bar is classesAfterMergingJitter >= 5 per settlement, minimum over the eight.

THE 3,284 UNTAGGED MESHES: the builder's refusal to tag them is UPHELD as correct, checked rather than taken on trust. The composition is published and reproducible via bypassComposition(), split four ways. The mechanism that would have laundered it — carryKitProvenance() — was built to prevent laundering and records how many batch members were NOT kit parts; a builder inclined to launder had the tool and used it in the honest direction. And the bulk of the number is not a tagging decision at all: ~9,945 public-realm meshes are plan item 6, declared not started, and tagging unstarted work would make an unbuilt thing report as built. The row stays FAIL because the bar is zero, but it fails for the right reason. Remedy: the builder's own suggestion — a 26th part for organic masses with the cap raised in writing and the count stated, or an explicit kitExempt tag the census counts separately from bypass so the public realm's 9,945 stop being averaged in with a design decision about blobs.

THE SKYLINE INDICATOR, PHOTOGRAPHED — and the answer is neither of the builder's two options. Its negative result stands (0.1835 shipped against 0.1862 flattened), and the frame says why: the skyline HAS relief — stepped roof masses, a tiered form and at least six masts breaking the roofline in Lilmoth — and the fog at the approach camera has removed almost all the contrast it needs to read. A statistic computed on untextured geometry with no sky and no fog cannot see that. So the offline indicator and the rendered frame disagree about the WORLD, not about the roofline. Consequence: the fog density at settlement-approach distance belongs to W1-30B, and E's approach row is BLOCKED rather than failed. Raise it as a defect-inventory row against B with approach-lilmoth__t1300__clear.jpg as its evidence, and re-run E's approach gate after it moves.

The edges-are-broken row passes with a nearly inert single-variable control. null:no-chamfer moves the metric 0.971 -> 0.9637 on a bar of 0.95 — the arm meant to remove the thing being measured leaves the row passing comfortably. The arm that does collapse it, kit:false at 0.4816, replaces the entire kit and confounds the chamfer with every other difference. The builder noticed half of this and introduced setKitChamfer(false), but the arm shipping in the gate output still reads 0.9637. The row is currently evidenced by the frames rather than by the statistic and its control. Remedy: make null:no-chamfer call setKitChamfer(false) and report that arm.

Said plainly because it is the best news in this verdict: the builder's reporting is unusually honest and nothing here overturns a number it reported. Four reds were declared on its own initiative; three control defects were self-found and self-corrected, including a first run in which ALL SIX arms produced identical values to four decimal places because the options never reached buildBuilding(), which the builder correctly read as evidence rather than as agreement. Every gate value and every control value reproduced to the last digit when re-run from the shipping tree by this critic.

corpus_extended.what: Four settlement roofline-relief rows on the art board are UNSET for want of plates — helstrom (n=2), archon (n=1), thorn (n=0), stormhold (n=0) — confirmed by re-running the board's own instrument, docs/art-direction/measure-plates.mjs. This is a corpus shortage, not a failure of this piece. No target was invented for them: the builder refused to and this critic refuses too. Owed: acquire reference plates for the four settlement profiles, or record in the board why those four cannot have a band.

The plan's roof-profile row is defective as written and Ruling E1 is the repair, but E1 needs to be written into the corpus rather than living only in a dispatch. Owed: append the silhouette reading to orchestration/plans/W1-30E.md's variation row with the aggregation stated (minimum over settlements, per Ruling W1) and the merge threshold named, so a later builder cannot read the row as counting kit parts and a later critic cannot read it as counting whole-building silhouettes. Both misreadings have already happened once each in this round.

method_deviations: The 12-shot unseen census sample was NOT drawn. The full Deck profile was captured instead, which is a superset of the fixed list but is not the census sample — the census sample's whole purpose is to be shots the builder could not anticipate, and drawing it is a separate seeded step. The anti-beauty-shot arm therefore did not run, and no claim in this verdict is protected by it.
The open defect inventory was not re-run, so this verdict does not report whether E's changes closed or opened rows in reports/visual-truth/INVENTORY.md.
WLD03's copy-paste matrix was not run.
Interior thresholds (plan item 7) were not examined against W1-30G's side of the doorway.
No naive attribution pack was built at either street or skyline range, for the S51 reason recorded against RI-VIS06 and RI-VIS07.
Draw calls were measured per settlement (106 worst), not frustum-scoped per street shot; the plan's <= 900 row remains CARRIED.

self_audit.self_audit_note: ran_every_assigned_method is FALSE and the misses are itemised in method_deviations; the two that matter most are the census sample, which is the anti-beauty-shot arm, and the naive attribution packs, which are this child's two primary rows. blind_done_where_required is FALSE for the S51 reason: pack-builder and judge must be different agents and this critic is one agent, so Protocol A is recorded at 0 with measured unmeasurable rather than being scored as a pass or quietly omitted. judged_output_not_source is TRUE — the gate was re-run rather than read, the falsifier was written against the shipping build's own geometry, and 288 frames were captured on real hardware. The one place this critic went to source first would have been wrong, so it did not: the roof-profile finding was demonstrated by the falsifier BEFORE kits.js was opened to explain it. The verdict also upholds two builder positions against the temptation to find a gap where none exists — the refusal to tag the 3,284 meshes, and the refusal to invent targets for the four UNSET board rows — because a critic may PASS a row without inventing a gap when the bar is evidenced.
